_comment: What a Blackwell GPU-hour rents for, and how it has moved. US dollars per GPU-hour throughout.
quotes: every published rental price this dashboard reads, normalised to one GPU-hour (instance price / GPUs): vendor, chip, tier
(on-demand | spot = interruptible / preemptible | capacity-block | reserved | index = a third-party index or aggregator),
'hyperscaler' marks AWS / Azure / Oracle / Google, 'pricing' says whether the vendor moves the price daily ('dynamic', e.g. Verda,
AWS Spot) or keeps a list ('list'). update.py refreshes every row whose 'refresh' block names a machine-readable source
(engine/collect_rentals.py documents each kind). 'status': 'not published' (the vendor shows 'Contact sales'), 'ended' (the
vendor stopped publishing the rate; 'ended' = the date), 'unverifiable' (the page blocks automated reads). 'announced' = a
published future price and its effective date. Every reading is kept in data/rate_history.json ('quotes').
changes: every price change the daily read saw (list prices on any move; dynamic prices at each 10% move since the last logged
value), plus dated changes documented by the vendor ('kind': 'stated'). notices: pricing notices found on the vendors' pages.
price_news: headlines about GPU price moves by the providers tracked (Google News, kept 60 days), unverified until confirmed.
price_actions: curated, sourced price moves that never reached a rate card (management disclosures, contract pricing per MW) or
that predate the daily collection. Edit by hand (or ask Claude).
contracts: every public multi-year AI compute contract found (Jan 2025 - Sep 2026), classified by 'kind': gpu-rental (a
neocloud sells GPU compute), cloud-commit (a lab commits spend to a hyperscaler), dc-lease (powered shell / colocation
hosting GPUs), backstop (NVIDIA rent-back guarantees), reference (third-party market quotes), expected, acv (stated
$/MW-year). per_gpu_hr = value / (term x 8760 x GPUs) where all three are disclosed ('computed'); per_mw_yr_musd =
value / (term x MW). 'use' marks the rows that enter the long-term contract medians: active GPU rentals (and market
references) on GB300 / B300 with a derivable rate. The daily 'deals' step queues new announcements in
data/deal_candidates.json for review; engine/deals_seed.py holds the seed list and the arithmetic.
The rental scenario's year-1 rate (assumptions.json rental.term_structure.near_term_basis) is by default the average of every
current GB300 / B300 rate in 'quotes' (spot, on-demand, capacity blocks; a rate is current for max_quote_age_days after it was
read); it converges to the long-term basis ('contract' = GPU-weighted median of the GB300-class contract rows by default).
